legend: Jubayer is a nice and talented kid. He is a two times ICPC World Finalist. He used to utilize his time solving problems after problems. But after all those years of hard work and achievements, he decides to enjoy a tiny break from his daily routine and roam to the villages of his very own B.Baria district. So, he went to B.Baria. But he soon became very fed up as he saw he cannot go to every village in his district as there are not enough roads that can help him reach every village. Also, a weird pattern was caught to the attention of this great programmer. In his district, there are n−1$$$n-1$$$ villages. The villages are named with natural numbers (don't ask me why, I am just a simple problem setter). For some weird reason, there is no village numbered as 1$$$1$$$. Villages are named from 2$$$2$$$ to n$$$n$$$ (for example: if n=5$$$n=5$$$ then name of the villages are 2$$$2$$$, 3$$$3$$$, 4$$$4$$$ and 5$$$5$$$). And there is a road connecting the village i$$$i$$$ and the village j$$$j$$$ if and only if either i$$$i$$$ is divisible by j$$$j$$$, or j$$$j$$$ is divisible by i$$$i$$$.

Now, Jubayer wishes to create some new roads to extend the reachability: he wants to connect every village and roam everywhere without any hassle. But he is failing to determine the minimum number of roads that he needs to construct in order to fulfill this purpose. Now it is your turn to help this world famous programmer.
input: First line will be number of test cases, T (1≤T≤105)$$$T\space(1 \le T \le 10^5)$$$.
Next T$$$T$$$ lines will have a number n (2≤n≤107)$$$n\space(2 \le n \le 10^7)$$$ denoting the name of the last village in the district.
output: For each test case, print the minimum number of roads needed to connect all the villages in a single line.
note: Explanation of the second test case:   Here n=5$$$n = 5$$$, so the villages are named 2,3,4,5$$$2,3,4,5$$$. There's already an edge between 2$$$2$$$ and 4$$$4$$$ because 2$$$2$$$ divides 4$$$4$$$.
You have to construct at least 2$$$2$$$ roads to make every village reachable to every other (via some roads).

legend.ai: Jubayer 是个善良又有才华的孩子。他曾两次入围 ICPC 世界总决赛。过去，他总是利用时间一道接一道地解题。但经过多年努力并取得诸多成就后，他决定暂时放下日常安排，去自己所在的 B.Baria 区的村庄逛逛。于是他去了 B.Baria。但很快他就感到十分沮丧，因为他发现区内的道路不足以让他到达每一个村庄。还有一个奇怪的规律引起了这位优秀程序员的注意。在他的区里有 n−1$$$n-1$$$ 个村庄。村庄用自然数命名(别问我为什么，我只是个普通的出题人)。出于某种奇怪的原因，没有编号为 1$$$1$$$ 的村庄。村庄的编号从 2$$$2$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$(例如：如果 n=5$$$n=5$$$，那么村庄的编号就是 2$$$2$$$、3$$$3$$$、4$$$4$$$ 和 5$$$5$$$)。当且仅当 i$$$i$$$ 能被 j$$$j$$$ 整除，或 j$$$j$$$ 能被 i$$$i$$$ 整除时，村庄 i$$$i$$$ 和村庄 j$$$j$$$ 之间有一条道路。
现在，Jubayer 希望修建一些新道路以扩大可达范围：他想连接每个村庄，并毫不费力地到处游历。但是，他无法确定为了实现这一目标需要修建的最少道路数量。现在轮到你来帮助这位世界闻名的程序员了。

input.ai: 第一行是测试用例数量 T(1≤T≤105)$$$T\space(1 \le T \le 10^5)$$$。
接下来 T$$$T$$$ 行中每行包含一个整数 n(2≤n≤107)$$$n\space(2 \le n \le 10^7)$$$，表示该地区最后一个村庄的名称。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，单独一行输出连接所有村庄所需的最少道路数量。

note.ai: 你必须修建至少 2$$$2$$$ 条道路，使得每个村庄都能通过一些道路到达其他任意村庄。
